newsitem.title: USA: MGM management completes $1.3 billion buyout.
newsitem.headline: MGM management completes $1.3 billion buyout.

text.p: A management-led group of executives, including billionaire Kirk Kerkorian, completed its $1.3 billion acquisition of the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc. film studio Thursday.

The group acquired the studio from France's state-owned Consortium de Realisation, the holding company formed to dispose of several assets of France's Credit Lyonnais and which became the owner of the studio under a bailout plan for the bank.
Credit Lyonnais had taken over the studio from Italian financier Giancarlo Parretti, who bought it in 1990 and later defaulted on loans.
The studio, founded in 1924, has produced some of the film industry's most acclaimed movies and enduring characters, such as "West Side Story," "Raging Bull" and 17 James Bond films.
But it fell on hard times after being acquired by Parretti, and eventually slipped into bankruptcy.

"We are now able to continue the dynamic creative environment fostered over the past three years and at last, clear away the cloud of uncertainty that has shadowed (MGM) for so long," MGM Chairman Frank Mancuso said in a statement.
Under Mancuso's leadership, the studio saw the successful distribution of films like "Leaving Las Vegas," "The Birdcage" and "Goldeneye," a James Bond film.

But Mancuso and the new group of owners face the immediate task of boosting both film and television production after the nearly year-long sale process that saw some Hollywood executives steer away from MGM until ownership was resolved.
Mancuso said the studio has slated production of some 13 to 14 films between now and the end of 1997. Within that time frame, he may acquire between three and four films for MGM.
He also must immediately replace John Calley, president of MGM's United Artists production wing, with an executive who can begin approving future film projects.
Calley announced his resignation from MGM earlier this week to take the co-president's position at Sony Corp.'s Sony Pictures Entertainment.

The deal to acquire MGM was sealed in a bidding process that ended in July when Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp and Australian media conglomerate Seven Network Ltd. offered their support for Mancuso's executive team.

Kerkorian has owned the studio twice before in its 72-year history, and his group is hopeful it can find synergy between the studio and the MGM Grand Inc. casino in Las Vegas, of which Kerkorian owns the majority.
Seven Network will use its stake in the studio to provide programming for its core broadcast television business in Australia and the Asia Pacific region.
